security_audit.summary: The skill is a Firebase development workflow document, not an executable package. Most findings are Markdown backticks, code examples, relative imports, and a localhost emulator URL. Several instructions ask the agent to run local shell commands, so those command findings remain confirmed.

remediation.issue: Shell commands are recommended without a trust boundary note.
remediation.suggestion: State that npm, Firebase CLI, and browser-open commands should run only in trusted Firebase workspaces after user confirmation.

remediation.issue: Npm scripts are used for build and test validation.
remediation.suggestion: Tell users to inspect package scripts before running npm commands in unfamiliar repositories.
Keep ls and grep scoped to project directories, and avoid commands that read secrets or home directories.

content.value_statement: Firebase feature work often misses tests, rules, and emulator validation. This skill guides Cloud Functions, Firestore changes, auth checks, and verification in one workflow.
actual_capabilities: Guides a 12-step workflow for new Firebase features.
Covers Cloud Functions, HTTP endpoints, callable functions, triggers, scheduled functions, and collections.
Provides TDD examples for unit and emulator integration tests.
Shows Firestore rules, indexes, auth checks, and response patterns.
Recommends emulator verification before marking work complete.
limitations: Requires an existing Firebase project and local toolchain.
Does not handle initial Firebase project setup.
Does not create deployment pipelines or production releases.
Uses placeholder names that must be adapted to the project.

use_cases.title: Add an API endpoint
use_cases.description: Create a new Express or Cloud Functions endpoint with tests, auth checks, and response validation.

use_cases.title: Create a Firestore collection
use_cases.description: Add a collection with security rules, indexes, and emulator checks before release.

use_cases.title: Standardize feature delivery
use_cases.description: Apply a repeatable checklist for tests, rules, exports, and emulator verification.

prompt_templates.title: Add a simple endpoint
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for one HTTP endpoint.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to add a Firebase HTTP endpoint for saving user preferences. Write the failing test first, then implement it.

prompt_templates.title: Create a collection
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate request for Firestore data modeling.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to add a Firestore collection for project notes. Include rules, indexes, unit tests, and emulator verification.

prompt_templates.title: Add authenticated logic
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to add an authenticated Cloud Function for team invitations. Follow the existing auth pattern and test denial cases.

prompt_templates.title: Deliver a complete workflow
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request spanning endpoint, storage, and tests.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to implement a complete Firebase feature for task assignments. Include handler logic, rules, indexes, exports, and integration tests.

output_examples.input: Add a user preferences endpoint to an existing Firebase app.
output_examples.output: A task checklist, failing unit test, handler implementation plan, auth requirement, Firestore rule update, and emulator verification steps.

output_examples.input: Create a new Firestore collection for project notes.
output_examples.output: A collection plan with owner-based rules, required composite index, test scenarios, and validation steps for the emulator suite.

output_examples.input: Add an authenticated Cloud Function for team invitations.
output_examples.output: A TDD workflow covering valid requests, rejected unauthenticated requests, exports, response format checks, and integration testing.

best_practices: Write the failing test before implementation work begins.
Match existing project architecture, auth patterns, and response conventions.
Verify behavior with Firebase emulators before marking the feature complete.
anti_patterns: Adding handlers before defining tests and expected behavior.
Creating Firestore collections without matching security rules.
Running npm scripts in unfamiliar repositories without reviewing them first.

faq.question: What Firebase work does this skill support?
faq.answer: It supports new Cloud Functions, endpoints, triggers, scheduled functions, callable functions, and Firestore collections.

faq.question: Does it require an existing Firebase project?
faq.answer: Yes. It assumes project structure, package scripts, and Firebase configuration already exist.

faq.question: Does it replace project setup guidance?
faq.answer: No. It is for feature additions after the Firebase project is already configured.

faq.question: How does it handle security rules?
faq.answer: It prompts updates to Firestore rules and asks for emulator verification of access behavior.

faq.question: Can it help with tests?
faq.answer: Yes. It emphasizes test-first development, unit tests, and emulator integration tests.

faq.question: Which AI tools can use it?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
